anti_overlap: Does not evaluate graph structure, embedding-based dedup methodology, or taxonomy-type semantics — that is fd-knowledgegraph-curation's territory
Does not evaluate discrimination-eval item/distractor design quality or eval construct validity — that is fd-psychometrics-itemvalidity's territory
Focuses on rater statistical validity, falsification-test design, and adjudication-attention economics, not on the graph's structural mechanics or the eval's item-quality mechanics
decision_lens: Treat the dual-rater edge-validation approach as an unproven hypothesis with a documented prior failure (dual-rater item labeling on this same domain) rather than an established method — ask what the cheapest test is that would surface a repeat failure before the plan commits the full 414-edge budget and mk's adjudication time to it.
focus: The dual-rater edge-validation bet, agreement-as-confidence statistics, and how mk's scarce adjudication attention should be allocated
name: fd-annotation-interrater
persona: Apply the perspective of a research methodologist specializing in annotation quality, inter-rater reliability, and human-in-the-loop / active-learning systems for label-scarce ML pipelines — someone who has run pilot studies to catch a repeated labeling failure before it burns the full annotation budget, and who is skeptical of agreement statistics computed without a chance-correction or base-rate check.
review_areas: Task-decontextualization argument: the plan's constraints section asserts that 'does a contrast relation exist between two lens definitions' is a more tractable, less situational task for an LLM rater than 'which lens fits this situation' — is this tested anywhere in the plan, or only asserted, and what would a decisive test look like?

Statistical soundness of confidence = inter-rater agreement between exactly two model families: with two raters, agreement is a binary agree/disagree per edge, and no chance-correction (e.g., Cohen's kappa or an explicit base-rate adjustment) is described — does this produce confidence scores meaningfully better than the 'decorative,' halo-prone scores the plan is explicitly trying to replace?

Falsifiability and pilot design: what is the cheapest test that would reveal whether dual-rater edge validation replicates the documented dual-rater item-labeling failure, and does the plan run it (e.g., against mk's 28 fresh ratings or the 14 split pairs as a held-out check) before scaling Phase C to all 414 contrasts edges?

mk's adjudication-attention allocation (the plan's open question 3): across the three candidate units — edges, node merges, generated items — what allocation rule does the plan implicitly or explicitly use, and is it defensible (e.g., route by disagreement rate or downstream leverage) versus default-to-everything routing that could exhaust the budget on low-leverage cases?

Whether committing mk's 28 fresh ratings and 14 split pairs as 'evidence, not gold' (a stated constraint) forfeits the one dataset in the whole plan with genuinely known-good labels — could a held-out comparison against these 28 ratings serve as exactly the falsification test Phase C needs before scaling?

Correlated-error risk: AgentWorld-35B (Qwen family) and GPT-OSS-120B (OpenAI family) are treated as independent raters because they are different model families, but do they share enough training-data or instruction-tuning bias toward common relation labels (e.g., both defaulting to 'complements' when uncertain) that agreement between them could still encode shared bias rather than independent confirmation?

severity_examples.condition: No pilot or held-out check against mk's existing 28 ratings gates entry into the full 414-edge Phase C pass.
severity_examples.scenario: Phase C runs dual-rater validation across all 414 contrasts edges before checking agreement against mk's 28 already-rated pairs as a pilot; the same 'models can't reliably do this task' failure that sank dual-rater item labeling recurs, and it is only discovered after the full edge-validation pass and its associated mk-adjudication load are spent.

severity_examples.condition: No chance-correction, base-rate check, or disagreement-pattern audit is applied to the two-rater agreement scores before they replace the existing confidence field.
severity_examples.scenario: The new dual-rater confidence field inherits the same halo problem it was built to replace, because both model families share a bias toward labeling ambiguous pairs as 'complements' by default, so agreement is high but not informative — the plan reports success (edges validated, confidence assigned) while the underlying ranking signal is still close to decorative.

severity_examples.condition: The plan specifies routing disagreements to mk but does not specify a prioritization or batching rule within that routing.
severity_examples.scenario: All Phase C and Phase D disagreements route to mk without a triage rule prioritizing high-leverage cases (e.g., edges that would seed many eval items), so mk's adjudication budget is spent roughly uniformly across edges regardless of downstream value, echoing the pattern that produced a 151-item candidate pool mk had to abandon.

success_hints: Explicitly tests the task-decontextualization claim in the constraints section rather than accepting it as given
Proposes a concrete, cheap pilot or falsification test using mk's existing 28 ratings or 14 split pairs before endorsing a full 414-edge Phase C pass
Addresses chance-correction or base-rate concerns for two-rater agreement specifically, not just 'two independent models agree, therefore confidence is sound'
Gives a reasoned, prioritized recommendation for allocating mk's adjudication attention across edges/merges/items rather than only flagging the allocation question as unresolved
Distinguishes correlated model bias from genuine independent confirmation when assessing the two-model-family design
task_context: This is a pre-ratification review of a plan (not yet a /goal) to overhaul the lens graph's curation quality before restarting discrimination-eval item generation from it. Review the plan's dual-rater edge-validation methodology and mk's adjudication-attention allocation specifically — the plan's own constraints section flags an open tension (dual-rater item labeling already failed in this domain) that it has not resolved. Stress the plan's central bets before mk ratifies it as a /goal: (1) that dual-rater edge validation will work where dual-rater item labeling already failed in this exact domain; (2) that graph-quality-first beats streaming/incremental restart of eval item generation; (3) that mk's adjudication attention (the scarcest resource) is spent on the right units — edges vs node merges vs generated items; (4) that the 4-type edge taxonomy is the right substrate for a discrimination eval at all. Surface missed alternatives and any cheaper falsification tests that should run before the full overhaul. A wrong call here wastes weeks of graph work and mk's labeling budget.
